Preliminary analysis — the board

First full pass over the 2026 campaign · 7–13 September 2026 · preliminary throughout

This is the working board for the first end-to-end analysis of the campaign, not a result. It holds four things: where we stand, the plan as a pipeline, what is deliberately not being done this week, and a dated log of what was decided along the way. The run quality assurance it stands on is finished and lives on its own four pages — nothing here re-does it.

Everything on this page is preliminary and internal. A number here has not been through a second pair of eyes unless the log entry beside it says so.

Where we stand

  • 0 Stages complete of 8 in the pipeline
  • 1 In progress what is being worked on right now
  • 0 Blocked waiting on something outside the week
  • 0 Open questions unresolved, listed below

The one-line status. The whole chain now runs end to end on the local development run and every stage has shipped a generated page: trigger → track → alignment → acceptance → opening angle. The geometry is in hand — the He-3 capsule is imaged at 9.3 mm off the beam axis, inside its own 10 mm bore, from a pointing crossing that needs no drift velocity, and the chamber-to-chamber spread of ±0.6 mm is the relative alignment. What is not in hand is statistics and one background: run 145’s 628 two-track pairs are consistent with accidentals in all three topologies, by a third independent route, and the accidental component has no normalisation yet because the trigger correlates the arms. The campaign pass is what turns the machinery into a measurement.

What this stands on

The four QA pages are finished and frozen. They are the inputs to everything below, and the analysis does not re-derive any of them — if a number here looks wrong, the fix belongs on the QA page, not on this one.

161 DREAM runs Every run the Micromegas DAQ recorded. 160 of 161 fully through the processing chain; the exception recorded no data. 445 n_TOF runs The facility’s own acquisition over the same beam, and whether each run’s partial set covers it. 99.99 % Beam pulses matched 279,938 of 279,972 matchable pulses on one clock, at the 60 % per-pulse bar. This is what makes an event an n_TOF event. 56 Pedestal sets The noise floor under all 4,096 channels, measured before every run — and the three things that moved during the campaign.

The plan, stage by stage

Each stage names what it produces — a file, a number, a plot — because a stage with no artefact cannot be called done. Later stages depend on earlier ones, but the order is the intended one, not a hard chain: several can run in parallel once the sample is frozen.

  1. Freeze the analysis sample

    Decide, once and in writing, which runs and which sub-runs enter the preliminary analysis — and write the list to a file every later stage reads. Beam runs only, ³He target, production trigger, fully processed and joined to n_TOF. Everything downstream quotes this list rather than re-selecting.

    • Producessample.csv — run, sub-run, file tag, n_TOF run, and the reason each was kept or cut, plus the beam-time timeline figure
    • ReadsDREAM QA, the match, pedestals
    • Watch forthe HV-scan runs — 64 of them swept a voltage mid-run and are not a fixed operating point; and run_79, whose arm-A x view needs channels 448–511 masked

  2. Time base and the flash veto

    Put every trigger on the n_TOF time-of-flight axis and decide where each event window usably begins. The gamma flash saturates the front end and the wall takes a known time to recover, so the start of the window is a cut, not a constant — and it is the cut that most directly sets how much beam survives. Comes before the filter, because the filter writes the flash time into every row.

    • Producesa per-trigger time-since-flash and En, and one stated veto window with the number it costs
    • Readsthe flash charge measurement, the clock QA
    • Watch forthe PSS ringing — a coherent artefact in the hit sample, vetoed before anything is counted

  3. The candidate filter

    Reconstructing 31 M triggers × four chambers blind is of order 105 core-hours, which is not a week. So every trigger is first classified from combined_hits alone — noise bands removed, hits clustered, clusters typed, track-like clusters counted per chamber — and crossed with which n_TOF arms saw a wall+plastic coincidence. One terminal class per trigger, so the ledger is a partition and every later efficiency has an honest denominator.

    • Producescandidates.parquet, one row per DREAM trigger (~31 M) — the class, the per-chamber cluster counts, the n_TOF arm flags, the flash time
    • ClassesINTER two chambers · INTRA two tracks in one · IMPLIED one chamber but two n_TOF arms · SINGLE · BUSY pile-up · NONE
    • Watch forthe filter's own efficiency is unmeasured going in — the prescaled control sample in the next stage is the only thing that measures it

  4. Reconstruct the candidates (WFT)

    The frozen waveform-first reconstruction, on condor, one job per (arm, file tag), with an event-id allowlist so only selected triggers are fitted. Everything in INTER, INTRA and IMPLIED — and for IMPLIED, the silent chamber too, forced — plus a prescaled control drawn from the rest. This is the expensive stage and the one that sets the week's pace.

    • Producesper-(arm, tag) track tables and the multi-track candidates sidecar, plus a completion ledger and a measured cost per 1,000 events
    • Needsthe sample frozen and the filter run; the calibration bundle pinned per chamber and per run condition, recorded in every row
    • Watch fordouble tracks closer than 12 mm fit as one bad-χ² compromise — they are flagged and counted, not recovered

  5. The track database

    X/Y pairing into 3D segments, into the global frame, with the crossed scintillator volumes predicted per track — and the n_TOF hits of the same event attached beside them. This is the artefact the week has to leave behind, because every later analysis reads it instead of re-running anything.

    • Producestracks.parquet (one row per 3D segment: geometry, quality, charge, timing, pointing, predictions, calibration provenance) and scint.parquet (one row per n_TOF hit, with the track predicted to have crossed it)
    • Rulenever collapse an ambiguity at write time — a two-track event's X↔Y pairing is genuinely ambiguous, so both hypotheses are written with their scores
    • Watch fora bundle used outside its conditions is a silent error; the row has to be able to say which bundle it is

  6. Scintillator positions

    Where a particle crossed the n_TOF scintillators. Across the wall: the segment that fired, four segments of 100 mm. Along the bar — the beam direction, since EAR2's beam is vertical — two independent estimators, the top–bottom transit time and the logarithm of the amplitude ratio. Both were characterised on n_TOF data alone; what is new is calibrating them against Micromegas tracks, which supply the truth the earlier study did not have.

    • Producesa fitted attenuation length and Δt scale per bar, a quoted position resolution, and the position column in scint.parquet
    • Needsthe track database, for the impact points
    • Watch for√(Atop·Abot) varies +9.1 % across a bar, and whether that is light collection or a reconstruction bias has never been separated

  7. Pair finding — intra, inter and implied

    From tracks to candidate pairs, in three topologies kept apart on purpose. Intra-chamber: two segments in one chamber, θ below ~90° — the continuum control. Inter-chamber: one segment in each of two chambers — the signal region, because an X17 opening angle of 109° or more cannot fit inside one chamber. Implied: one good track plus an n_TOF coincidence in a second arm that produced no track, which is how a chamber-B or chamber-D miss is recovered. Every cut gets a line in a cutflow table.

    • Producespairs.parquet and a cutflow per topology, quoted in every later plot
    • Needsthe database; and for the implied topology, a measured false-positive rate from the accidental two-arm rate and from a blinded control
    • Watch forthe four arms are not equivalent — B and D are tagging chambers this week, and any pair using their angle is reported separately from an A×C one

  8. The opening-angle spectrum

    The headline distribution, uncorrected: opening angle per candidate pair, one spectrum per topology. Plotted first with no acceptance correction and no background subtraction, so that what the correction and the subtraction each do is visible rather than assumed. No invariant mass — that needs an energy calibration we do not have.

    • Producesthe raw opening-angle spectra with their statistical errors, and the numbers behind them as CSV
    • Needspair finding
    • Watch forbinning chosen once and stated, not tuned after the fact

  9. Acceptance and efficiency

    A straight-line toy through the as-built active-volume model: pairs thrown from the capsule with a flat opening-angle distribution, folded with the per-chamber reconstruction efficiency measured on the control sample. Geometry only this week — no multiple scattering. The active area is measured, not assumed.

    • Producesa correction curve versus opening angle, per topology, with the geometry it assumes stated
    • Readsthe measured active area
    • Watch forthe trigger efficiency is a separate factor from the geometric one; keep them separable

  10. Backgrounds

    What else makes two tracks that look like a pair. The accidental rate from event mixing across bunches; the cosmic rate straight off the beam-off runs taken at the production operating point; the flash-induced residual from the veto sideband. All data-driven, and the accidental estimate comes first because it needs nothing from simulation.

    • Producesone background shape per component, normalised, and their sum against the raw spectrum
    • Needspair finding for the shape; the time base for the off-time window
    • Watch fora background normalised to the same data it is subtracted from will always fit

  11. The preliminary picture

    Corrected spectra, background subtracted, with the IPC expectation overlaid — and an honest statement of what the sample can and cannot say. If the answer this week is “the statistics do not reach the question”, that is the result and it gets written down as one.

    • Producesthe summary figures, sized for a projected slide, and a note published beside this board
    • Needsthe spectrum, the acceptance and the backgrounds
    • Watch forno systematic uncertainty is being claimed this week — say so on the plot

Not this week

Deliberately out of scope for the preliminary pass. Each item says why it is deferred and what would unblock it, so that nothing here can be mistaken for an oversight.

  • Systematic uncertaintiesdeferred Why: a preliminary spectrum with a full systematic budget takes longer than a week, and a half-done budget is worse than a stated absence. Unblocked by: the statistical picture settling first — the budget should be built against a spectrum that is not going to move.
  • Per-channel gain calibrationdeferred Why: the preliminary pass uses one gain per chamber. Per-channel gain changes resolution, not the presence or absence of a peak. Unblocked by: the pedestal and threshold work already on the QA page, plus a pass over the pulser runs.
  • The HV-scan runsdeferred Why: 64 runs swept a voltage mid-run, so they have no single operating point and cannot enter a sample that assumes one. Unblocked by: splitting them at the setpoint boundaries — worth doing, and worth roughly a quarter of the campaign’s runs.
  • Cosmic-bench cross-calibrationdeferred Why: the June fleet characterisation is finished and published, but folding its per-detector resolution into the n_TOF chambers is its own study. Unblocked by: nothing external — it is a time cost, not a dependency.
  • Merged-cluster double tracks (D1)deferred Why: two tracks closer than 12 mm fit as one bad-chi2 compromise, but they are flagged quality_ok=False and counted, so the loss is measured rather than silent Unblocked by: a two-column NNLS design matrix in wft/model.py plus a 1-vs-2-track model-selection penalty
  • Simulating the double-track finding efficiency (D2)deferred Why: we can say we lose some merged pairs, not how many. It does not block a preliminary spectrum, it blocks calling one a measurement Unblocked by: Geant4 pairs pushed through the response sim and the full chain, binned by opening angle and track separation. The most valuable single item on this list
  • Breaking the X-Y pairing ambiguity for simultaneous tracks (D3)deferred Why: for a two-track event, which x goes with which y is genuinely degenerate; this week writes both hypotheses and quotes the spread as a systematic Unblocked by: two handles already in the schema and unused: whether the pairing points back at the He-3 sample, and whether the two projections carry the same charge profile
  • Calibrating chambers B and D (D4)deferred Why: their in-situ angle scale is unphysical (k = 1.99 and 1.70, drift velocities down to 21 um/ns against a 42.6 prior), and B truncates 46-56 percent of its columns. They enter as tagging chambers only Unblocked by: a dedicated per-chamber study. This is the biggest single limit on the signal region, since the X17 topology needs one of them in most events
  • In-situ drift velocity and diffusion (D9)deferred Why: the chain still runs on values transferred from the June bench, which is the largest unvalidated assumption in it. A wrong v scales angles, it does not invent a peak Unblocked by: porting the stacked-NNLS erfc-endpoint gap study to the beam runs; it costs no refit
  • dE/dx in the Micromegas (D5)deferred Why: gain variation across a chamber is expected to dominate, so a dE/dx number now would measure the gain map rather than the ionisation Unblocked by: a per-region gain map from the pulser and source runs
  • Scintillator energy calibration and calorimetry (D6)deferred Why: this is what would unlock the invariant mass, and it is a project rather than a task. Without it the deliverable is the opening angle alone Unblocked by: an energy scale for the plastics, the SiPM wall and the liquids, each verified before use
  • Liquid scintillator gain across the surface (D7)deferred Why: no liquid amplitude is used as energy this week, so the gain map does not bite yet Unblocked by: measuring how far the gain moves with distance from the PMT and across the surface, with Micromegas tracks defining the impact point
  • The neutron-energy axis (D11)deferred Why: time-since-flash is already written into every row, so nothing is lost by not analysing it this week Unblocked by: the opening-angle spectrum resolved in E_n, once there are enough pairs to bin twice
  • Absolute alignment (D8)deferred Why: arms A and C agree on a source 9 mm off axis, and whether that is a real target offset or a survey error cannot be separated by more tracks. Positions are quoted to about 1 cm and that is enough for an angle Unblocked by: survey information, or an independent beam-spot measurement
  • Beam-side kernel calibration (a ref-free training selector)deferred Why: wft.calibrate is ref-pinned to the M3 telescope, which the beam does not have, so this is new development rather than a re-run -- and only chamber B currently needs it Unblocked by: a training selector that pins on the target constraint tan = (u - foot)/d_perp instead of on a reference ray

Open questions

Things that have to be decided before a later stage can be called done. A question that gets answered stays here with its answer attached.

  • Does the preliminary sample take the whole campaign, or only the runs after the 23 July pedestal step? The noise floor doubled on that date, and mixing the two epochs mixes two thresholds.

    opened 2026-09-07

    Resolved 2026-09-07: Only the production period: run_79 onward. run_67 is the quiet pre-23-July noise configuration and run_68 sits inside the pedestal bracket unplaced, so neither can be pooled with the rest. run_79 itself is kept but flagged - its arm-A x view needs channels 448-511 masked.

  • Is the flash veto one window for the whole campaign, or per chamber? Chamber A behaved differently through the pedestal history, and a single window would be set by the worst arm.

    opened 2026-09-07

  • What is the minimum sample size that makes the opening-angle spectrum worth plotting at all? Worth deciding before the reconstruction runs, not after.

    opened 2026-09-07

  • Can chambers B and D be rescued for the preliminary, or do they stay tagging-only? An X17 opening angle is at least 109 degrees and one chamber subtends about 40, so the signal topology needs one of them in most events - which makes their uncalibrated angle scale the binding constraint on the whole measurement.

    opened 2026-09-07

    Resolved 2026-09-07: Partly. D is rescued: on an interquartile charge window its three angle-scale estimators agree to 11% and reproduce to 3%, k = 1.751 (v 24.3 um/ns), so D now carries angles like A and C. B is not: its focus objective never turns over across the whole scan grid and its k jumps 1.35 to 2.30 depending on the charge window, so B stays tagging-only. B can still serve as a TRIGGER control in the pair analysis, since the trigger arm comes from the n_TOF slim rather than from the reconstruction.

  • Are implied pairs - one real track plus an n_TOF coincidence in a chamber that saw nothing - good enough to appear on the same plot as measured pairs, or only in a figure of their own? Turns on the false-positive rate, which is measurable from the accidental two-arm rate and from a blinded control.

    opened 2026-09-07

  • Does run_79 get masked, reweighted, or quoted separately in the campaign census? Its chamber-A x plane is 2.5x noisier than the rest of the campaign and it inflates INTER, INTRA and BUSY together. It is 16 of 293 sub-runs.

    opened 2026-09-08

  • Chamber D reads the scintillator wall backwards -- is it D's two wall ends swapped in the readout map, or D's Micromegas y strip plane mirrored? Both estimators flip together, so it is one flip somewhere in D's chain, and the data cannot say which link. D's own wall self-check is the strongest of the four (r = -0.83), and its shallow slope is what noise in the predictor does, both pointing at the Micromegas side; run_config declares the same FEU orientation for all four chambers, so an MM-side mirror would have to be an undeclared cabling difference. What would settle it is an external fact: the wall cabling map, or the y-plane strip mapping order, for arm D.

    opened 2026-09-08

  • How do we normalise the accidental pair background? The mixed sample gives the shape but no rate, and the Poisson product over-predicts by 2-4x because the trigger correlates the arms. The two-chamber rate solved the same problem with a control chamber -- does that transfer to a differential spectrum, or does it need an unbiased trigger sample?

    opened 2026-09-08

  • The capsule looks +22 mm high in y and ~9 mm off in X, and all chambers agree on both. Is that the target really sitting there, or a shared convention error in the strip-map origin? Three physically independent detectors sharing an offset argues for a convention; nothing in the tracks separates them. Needs survey information or a beam-spot measurement.

    opened 2026-09-08

  • 2026-09-08

    The pair background has no normalisation yet, and both candidates were measured to fail. The event-mixed sample is built pair-for-pair with the data, so subtracting all of it subtracts the signal -- it is a shape template and carries no rate. The Poisson product N_trig * p_i * p_j over-predicts the observed pair count by 2.0-4.2x in every arm combination, because the production trigger is a wall-and-plastic coincidence in one arm and that correlates the arms. A control chamber, as pairs.py already uses for the two-chamber rate, is the highest-value next step for the spectrum.

    background · spectrum

  • 2026-09-08

    The opening angle, put against an expectation for the first time -- and run_145's pairs are accidentals. A pair generator reproduces the full Geant4 sample to KS = 0.002 (X17) and 0.003 (IPC) under Geant's own assumptions, then varies them: the 4He 0+ -> 0+ transition is E0 and emits a LONGITUDINAL virtual photon (sin^2 theta*), not the isotropic one the generator assumes, so the IPC continuum is carried as a band. An acceptance toy thrown flat in opening angle from the S2-measured capsule position collapses ~6x across the middle. Folding them and comparing in three topologies, the event-mixed shape fits every one at chi2/dof 1.8-3.1 while the best genuine pair spectrum manages 6.7 and worse. Third independent route to the same null. the opening-angle page

    CORRECTION: chamber B does contribute an alignment point, and N2 explains no chamber. B has no field cage, so it has no angle scale and never will -- but the pointing crossing asks only where the reconstructed angle is zero, which a distorted but symmetric field still puts in the right place. B gives global Z at +-2 mm, so Z is cross-checked rather than single-sided. Separately, the first version of the gas-chain note said 5 % N2 could account for chamber A; it cannot -- that mixture drifts at 35.2 um/ns, above all three measured chambers. The inversion returning NaN is what caught it.

  • 2026-09-08

    The He-3 capsule is imaged at X = -8.4, Z = -4.1 mm -- 9.3 mm off the beam axis, inside its own 10 mm bore. The pointing band's zero crossing is scale-free, so this survives every doubt in the drift velocity, k and the bundle. A and C measure global X from opposite sides and agree to 1.1 mm; the chamber-to-chamber spread of +-0.6 mm IS the relative alignment. y has no crossing and comes from the distribution against a gas-polycone forward model: +22 mm, shared by all three chambers, with a resolution of 44-109 mm. the source-imaging page

    alignment · geometry

  • 2026-09-08

    The n_TOF scintillators are a filter and nothing else -- and the wall is a 53 mm position detector nobody was reading. Three roles (stage-1 class, efficiency denominator, funnel pointing) share three branches and every answer is boolean. But each wall group appears in the slim as two detn values, the two ends of the same four bars, and the bars run along the beam axis: delay and attenuation both measure position along them. They agree with each other at r = -0.69 to -0.83 in all four chambers including B, with no Micromegas in the argument, and against MM tracks the wall localises to sigma_y < 53 mm on a 500 mm bar. Needs no reprocessing and no EOS. the scintillator page

    scintillators · measurement

  • 2026-09-08

    Drift velocity falls monotonically down the gas line, and it is water. All four chambers held the same 700 V through run_145 (E = 233 V/cm, read from the run's own hv_monitor.csv), so the ladder 33.6 -> 26.4 -> 24.2 um/ns for A -> C -> D cannot be field: it is the signature of pickup along the single daisy-chained line A -> B -> C -> D. Inverted against the Magboltz suite at the measured field it is 0.37 / 0.67 / 0.77 % H2O. O2 and air are excluded by attachment (they would strip the cathode-side charge, which run58 measured flat), and N2 cannot reach even the driest chamber -- 5 % N2 still drifts at 35.2 um/ns. the funnel report, section 3b

    gas · calibration

  • 2026-09-08

    Chamber D has ~130 dead readout channels of 512 -- a quarter of its x plane -- clustered on connector boundaries (ch 183-212, 219-227, 234-255 on connectors 2-3, plus ch 27-63 on connector 0). Same class of fault as chamber A's connector-8 outage in run_79. Chamber C has one small dead run (ch 227-236); chamber A has none. This CORRECTS an explanation I committed earlier: I read the central gap in the filtered hit maps as the reconstruction blanking normal-incidence tracks via TAN_MIN_SLOPE, and it is not -- the 3D gate never uses slope_reliable, and the gaps are present in the raw occupancy before any selection. D's angle scale survives regardless: re-measured with the outer ring excluded it moves 2% and the estimator spread improves, because the pointing coincidence already strips the edge junk (44.1% of D's fitted clusters are in the outer ring against 6.8% of its k sample).

  • 2026-09-08

    Campaign census under way, and its first full sub-run validates the method. run_79/stat090_0006 -- 14 tags, 109,272 triggers, 13x the earlier single-tag spot check -- gives INTER 2.00%, INTRA 5.40%, BUSY 2.56%, NONE 73.82% against the spot check's 1.86 / 5.73 / 2.64 / 72.95%. Agreement to ~7% on every class, so the single-tag sampling that the campaign-homogeneity comparison rests on is sound, and run_79's excess is real at full statistics rather than a small-sample effect. Its INTER events carry a median 409 clean strips against run_145's 162 -- the same noisier state the per-arm busy rates showed. The census is streamed and resumable, 8 workers, ~45 min per sub-run, so 293 sub-runs is a multi-night job: 'bash sept26_prelim_analysis/campaign_census.sh --status' for progress, and re-running it continues where it stopped.

  • 2026-09-08

    A beam-side kernel refit is development, not a re-run -- and all four bundles are bench transfers. wft.calibrate.build_cache is REF-PINNED: it selects training events along the M3 reference corridor and fits the model against per-event reference track parameters as truth. The beam has no reference telescope, so it cannot run there at all. This also corrects an assumption: arm C's bundle provenance reads 'fitted: wft.calibrate' but that describes its parent BENCH fit -- the same record says 'transferred: template + sharing kernel + w0/kw (bench)'. No bundle has ever been fitted on beam data. What would make it possible is a ref-free training selector: the beam has a constraint the bench does not, a point source 234.6 mm away making position and angle dependent, which is the relation k_arm already uses to measure the angle scale. A calibration could pin on the target the same way.

    calibration · method · decision

  • 2026-09-08

    Chamber B: a fourth suspect eliminated, and the wall readout order independently confirmed. The conditional funnel shows B's loss is diffuse rather than at one stage, with one exception -- pointing confirmation per gated track splits the chambers into pairs, A 35.9% and C 28.9% against B 10.1% and D 11.6%, which is exactly X-view against Z-view. Since the wall order was originally measured by maximising the coincidence, an order determined on the X pair and applied blindly to the Z pair was a real possibility. It is not that: trying all four orderings of wall segment and plastic bar, ascending/ascending wins in every chamber (A 44.8, B 20.5, C 35.6, D 15.0 %) and every reversal collapses to 2-6 %. So statistics, scan range, charge window and readout order are all out, and B's only real distinction from D -- which does certify -- is yield: 412 tracks against 933 after the charge window, where 412 is demonstrably enough for A and D. B's tracks carry less angle information per track, which points at the bench-transferred sharing kernel. Next step is a beam-side kernel refit for B.

  • 2026-09-08

    Stage 1 validated outside run_145, and the campaign is homogeneous. Four single-tag censuses spanning six weeks: run_116 (31 Jul), run_145 (5 Aug) and run_162 (9 Aug) agree to a few percent on every class -- INTER 0.96/1.01/0.98 %, BUSY 1.20/1.27/1.15 % -- inside the ~10 % single-tag sampling error measured from run_145's own one-tag vs all-tag census. So run_145 is representative of the bulk. run_79 (26 Jul) is the outlier: INTER 1.86 %, INTRA 5.73 %, BUSY 2.64 %, driven by chamber A being busy in 9.2 % of triggers against 1.4-1.6 % later. It is NOT the dead A-x connector -- those channels fire at 0.3x the per-channel rate of the rest of their FEU with 23 of 64 alive, exactly as a partly disconnected connector should. The rest of that FEU is what is elevated, 2.5x per channel: A's x plane was broadly noisier in run_79, not locally broken, and it had recovered by 31 July with the 27 July access in between.

  • 2026-09-07

    The pair null now has its dominant systematic, and it is larger than any apparent excess. Running the same controlled comparison against each perpendicular chamber ALONE instead of pooled moves the significance by up to 3.4 sigma -- chamber D's excess is +3.4 sigma against control A and +0.7 sigma against control C, at the same target cut on the same events. Nothing in the pair table sits outside that, which settles the null more firmly than the symmetry argument alone. Combined A-C limit: second-track rate below 0.07-0.12% of triggers at 95% CL.

    physics · systematics

  • 2026-09-07

    The two-chamber null now carries a sensitivity. Combining both directions of the A-C pair inverse-variance -- the same physics measured twice, and a real signal cannot average away while an acceptance asymmetry can -- the excess is +1.5 +- 11.2 events (0.14 sigma) at a 20 mm target cut, +12.9 +- 13.7 (0.95 sigma) at 30 mm and +5.7 +- 18.2 (0.31 sigma) at 50 mm. The 95% CL upper limit on the second-track rate is 0.07 to 0.12 % of triggers, over 118,190 single-arm triggers of run_145. That the combination averages the per-direction +2.0 and -1.5 sigma to 0.1 sigma is the check that the asymmetry was acceptance. the report

    physics · result

  • 2026-09-07

    End-to-end geometry validated, for free, from the two-chamber events. Two tracks from the target into OPPOSING chambers must open wide and into PERPENDICULAR ones ~90 deg -- and they do: A-C median 144 deg with essentially no density below 95 deg, against A-D 83 deg and C-D 97 deg, both falling away above 120 deg. That single separation validates the strip maps, both in-plane signs, the pinwheel, the chamber transforms and the angle scale together. It is not a pair signal; the controlled rate is null. the figure

    geometry · validation

  • 2026-09-07

    Chamber B closed out with three tests, and it is not fixable by more data. (1) Not statistics: subsampled to B's 412 tracks, A recovers its angle scale to +-0.03 and D to +-0.06, with plateau widths of 0.35-0.45 against B's 0.75. (2) Not the scan range: with the grid opened to k=6, B peaks at 2.10 in one sub-run and 4.45 in the other (v 20 vs 10 um/ns) while A gives 1.20/1.20. (3) Not the charge window: B's k jumps 1.35 to 2.30 across windows where A, C and D move less than a plateau width. On the full gated sample B is uniform across all 15 tags at ~39 strips and chi2/dof ~16.5 -- its multiplicity tracks its bundle's kY, so the likely cause is the bench-transferred sharing kernel not describing B in the beam. D shares the high kY and worse chi2/dof and still certifies, so multiplicity alone is not it.

    detectors · calibration

  • 2026-09-07

    Chamber D re-certified -- three of four chambers now carry angles. The pointing-band estimator was failing on D because its LOWEST-chi2 quarter anti-points (corr -0.43) while the other three point correctly: low chi2/dof there means 'nothing to fit', so a chi2 cut selects the noise-fits rather than removing them. Banding by CHARGE separates them (D runs -0.01/+0.56/+0.71/+0.13 across charge quartiles -- noise at the bottom, saturation at the top), and on the interquartile charge window D's estimator spread falls from 92% to 11%: k = 1.751, v = 24.3 um/ns. Not a tuned cut -- the focus estimator moves less than a plateau width as the window is opened all the way to 0-100. B stays out: its focus k jumps 1.35 to 2.30 across windows, which is B having no stable optimum.

    calibration · detectors · decision

  • 2026-09-07

    Controlled two-chamber measurement built and run on run_145: null at the ~1% ambient level. Only A and C have angles, and they are the opposing pair, so A-C is the one X17-topology channel currently measurable

    stage: pairing

  • 2026-09-07

    First CONTROLLED two-chamber measurement, and it is null. The direct count is meaningless because the trigger fires on one arm and so partitions events by arm -- the A-pointing and C-pointing event sets overlap 3.5x LESS than independent expectation, so any excess quoted against a product-of-marginals null measures the trigger. The controlled version fixes the track chamber and varies the trigger chamber (B and D serve as controls even without usable angles, since the trigger arm comes from the slim). Over 118,190 single-arm triggers the two directions have OPPOSITE signs at every dca cut: A-track/C-trigger +2.0/+1.8/+2.7 sigma, C-track/A-trigger -1.5/-0.4/-2.1 sigma. A back-to-back signal must be symmetric, so this is an A-vs-C acceptance asymmetry, not a pair.

    physics · result · decision

  • 2026-09-07

    The Y strip coordinate needed the same in-plane sign flip as X, and never got it. The 2026-08-20 sign measurement was made on the target image, which lives in the XZ projection and is blind to the y sign, so only x was measured -- every 3D track direction has carried a mirrored vertical component since. corr(y_local, tan_y) must be positive for a source-pointing track; unflipped it is negative in all four chambers and both run_145 sub-runs, flipped it is positive in all eight. Independent check: the flip moves the median target height from below the He-3 capsule to near its centre (A -7.6 to +16.4 mm, capsule spans -29.5 to +50.7) and roughly doubles the fraction pointing into its y span. Affects opening angles between chambers; dca in XZ barely notices, which is why it survived.

    geometry · bug · decision

  • 2026-09-07

    Partial answer on B and D. D is one fit away from usable: its per-track and focus estimates of the angle scale agree to 0.7% (1.713, 1.725) and only the pointing-band fit fails, at 3.29. B is a different problem -- its focus objective rises monotonically across the whole scan grid (k = 0.60 to 2.55) and never turns over, so B carries no angle information at all. Both keep null angles for now; D is the first candidate for re-certification.

    detectors · calibration

  • 2026-09-07

    The stage-2 allowlist sample is background-dominated, and the angle scale exposed it. Applying the measured k makes the median target miss WORSE on that sample (A 54.6 -> 56.7 mm, C 79.4 -> 99.8 mm), and its own best k is ~1.1 for every chamber regardless of which chamber it is -- i.e. it carries almost no target-track information. On the pointing-coincident sample the optima are sharp and chamber-specific. Anything measured on the allowlist sample alone inherits this, the two-chamber excess included.

    reconstruction · caution

  • 2026-09-07

    The reconstruction funnel is published, built on the FULL waveform pass so no number inherits a hits-based selection. 122,280 triggers -> 75,473 gated 3D tracks -> 15,398 pointing-confirmed. Every chamber confirms wall+plastic more often than its own no-track control (lift 1.15x to 1.49x), so the tracking selects real particles rather than following the trigger. Two flags: D seeds 80% of triggers against 37-40% for the others and confirms worst, and LIQ C is effectively dead in run_145 (891 in-time hits against 7,227 in A). the report

    reconstruction · qa

  • 2026-09-07

    Two methodological traps found in run145_target_imaging, both now avoided. k_phys is set to k_track_coincident verbatim, so reading it as a third opinion double-counts one estimator; and k_opt minimises r_core, a median conditioned on a cut that k itself moves, which can be improved by shrinking the core rather than focusing it. sept26_prelim_analysis/k_arm.py re-derives the focus estimator as a count inside a FIXED radius and reports the plateau -- the range of k the data cannot separate.

    calibration · method

  • 2026-09-07

    Angle scale measured in situ. tan = w/v: the fit measures a transverse speed, v was a Magboltz prior (42.6 um/ns) never measured in these chambers. k = v_prior/v_true from three estimators whose failure modes do not overlap -- pointing-band slope, per-track ratio, focus scan -- on the pointing-coincident sample. A k=1.25 (v 34) and C k=1.58 (v 27) provisional and applied; B and D not calibrated and carrying NULL angles rather than a silent k=1. Every chamber drifts slower than the prior. the funnel report

    logistics

  • 2026-09-07

    Named the topologies properly, and it changes the priorities. An X17 at 16.8 MeV produced at 20.58 MeV has a minimum opening angle of 109 degrees; one chamber subtends about plus-minus 40. So a pair inside a single chamber cannot be signal - that topology is the low-angle IPC control - and the signal is one track in each of two chambers, which in this geometry usually means one of A or C paired with one of B or D. The two chambers whose angle scale is unphysical are on the critical path.

    physics · decision

  • 2026-09-07

    Plan of record written. The chain is sample - time base - hits-level candidate filter - WFT reconstruction on what survives - track database - scintillator positions - pair finding - spectrum. The filter is the load-bearing decision: reconstructing 31.2 M triggers across four chambers blind is of order 100,000 core-hours, and filtering on combined_hits first is what makes the week possible. run_145 is the local development run - post-23-July, post-run_83, already reconstructed on all four arms, and its A-C pointing agreement at 9 mm is the sanity check the rebuilt chain has to reproduce.

    plan · decision

    Board opened. The pipeline below is the plan as written on day one, before anything has been run against a frozen sample — expect the middle stages to change shape once the reconstruction cost is known.

What came out of it

Notes, plots and child pages produced during the week. A row with no link is written but not yet published; publishing one is scripts/add-note.py, and then this row becomes a link.

  • The opening angle, against an expectationlive Physics x acceptance in three topologies: a validated pair generator, a geometric toy, and pairs that look like accidentals.
  • Imaging the He-3 capsulelive Where the source is from the scale-free pointing crossing, and what the chambers' disagreement is worth as alignment.
  • Scintillators: filter, or measurement?live What the n_TOF detectors contribute today (a yes/no, in three places) and the position along the wall bars nobody was reading.
  • X17 preliminary analysis — plan and statuslive The plan of record as a written note: the chain stage by stage, what it will not establish, and what is deferred to October. This board tracks the same work day to day; the note is the version to cite.
  • The preliminary analysis planplan The plan of record for the week of 8 September: the chain stage by stage, the four conditions that would silently bias a number, what the week will not establish, and the fifteen-item register of what is deferred to October.

How to update this page

Two ways, both fine

  • Edit the fragment The page is ordinary hand-written HTML at pages/x17/analysis.html. Change a stage’s data-status, rewrite a paragraph, add a section — then python3 scripts/build.py and ./scripts/deploy-eos.sh. Nothing here is generated from data, so there is no schema to fight.
  • Use the helper, from any repo For the repetitive parts — x17_board.py log "…", question, defer, stage <slug> --status done, output — which edit the same fragment in place and rebuild. --deploy pushes. It exists so a session in the analysis repo can add an entry without opening this one.
